_comment: Template for the gitignored mcp/vault-map.local.json used by bin/mcp-run.sh.
Maps each MCP server's expected environment variables to the vault item
that holds the secret. Item identifiers and tenant names are why the real
file is gitignored (docs/client-data-policy.md) — keep this template free
of both.
Top-level key = server name: either mcp/<server>-mcp-server.py in this
repo, or an entry in mcp/external-servers.json for a server installed
outside it.
Value = {ENV_VAR: {item, field}}. 'field' is one of password | username |
notes | <custom field name>, and defaults to password when omitted.
Which variables a server expects is documented in its own module
docstring. Three examples:
technitium — one password per DNS server, named by that server's
'env_pass' key in tenants-technitium.local.json
erpnext    — ERPNEXT_API_KEY_<TENANT> and ERPNEXT_API_SECRET_<TENANT>
per tenant in tenants.local.json (token auth against a
low-privilege service account — never an admin password).
Store the api_key and the BARE api_secret as two fields,
never the full 'key:secret' token: token auth builds
'Authorization: token <key>:<secret>', so a full token
becomes 'token key:key:secret' and 401s (see
docs/erpnext-mcp-setup.md).
wireguard  — password + TOTP seed per environment, named by that
environment's 'env_pass' / 'env_totp' keys in
tenants-wireguard.local.json. Note field 'totp': it exports
the item's TOTP *seed* so the server can derive a fresh code
per request. A dashboard with 2FA rejects a password-only
login with a message that blames the password (opskit #90).
proxmox    — the FULL token identity (user@realm!tokenname) from the
item's username, plus the token value from its password.
mcp/proxmox-mcp-server.py splits the identity, so the map
stays one-field-to-one-variable with no transforms.
mikromcp   — external (mcp/external-servers.json). One <PREFIX>_USER /
<PREFIX>_PASS pair per router, where <PREFIX> is that
router's 'envPrefix' in ~/.mikromcp/routers.yaml. mikromcp
declares a credentials.source of "vault" in its schema but
does not implement it (VAULT_NOT_SUPPORTED), which is why
resolution happens in the launcher instead. Prefer a scoped
read-only RouterOS API user over a router admin account —
REST is plaintext HTTP until www-ssl is enabled (opskit #94).
